title: "Analyses — twelve questions about the 2026 war"

The twelve questions are organized as a causal arc through the war. Each section answers a distinct phase or layer of the conflict. Sections can be read independently — no prescribed order beyond the arc itself.

## Project notes

**On Q-numbers.** The Q-numbers are stable identifiers carried over from the analytical source files; they are not narrative ordering. Reading order follows the section headings above, not the question numbers.

**On Q4.** The original Q4 ("what sustains the coalitions?") was answered through cross-coverage in Q11 (US-Israel), Q12.4 / Q12.5 (Gulf), Q9 (Europe-US), Q2 (Iran-side regime-survival as proxy network's structural driver), and Q7 (Russia-NK supply chain). With the original question fully addressed, Q4 was redefined as the operational-feasibility analysis of the US-led counter-blockade — the only major operational question the existing chapters did not engage directly.

**On Q12 sub-questions.** The Gulf is a distinct analytical focus because the standard frame (the GCC as a single bloc) does not fit the observed behavior. Three additional Q12 sub-questions are drafted in the analytical source but do not have dedicated chapter pages: Q12.1 (how should the Gulf neighbors be sub-grouped?); Q12.2 (how did each sub-group's strategy evolve from JCPOA → 2023 rapprochement → February 2026?); Q12.3 (how did Iran's Hormuz weapon shape pre-war Gulf strategy?). Their content is largely absorbed into Q12.4, Q12.5, and Q10.
